title: Living on Borrowed Identity
tagline: Some debts don't show up on statements, but they still control your life.
seo_title: Spiritual Debt: Living on Borrowed Identity | Romans 13:8 for Men | TheWrkShop
seo_description: You can be financially stable and still be spiritually leveraged. A devotional on Romans 13:8 and 12:1-2 about the approval, image and control men keep paying for.
verse_text: Let no debt remain outstanding, except the continuing debt to love one another.

scriptures.text: Let no debt remain outstanding, except the continuing debt to love one another.
Offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God. Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.

blocks.text: Most men think debt is just numbers: balances, interest rates, monthly payments.
But Scripture expands the definition. You can be financially stable and still be spiritually leveraged.
This isn't just about money. It's about ownership, obligation and freedom.
Debt works like this: you borrow today and repay tomorrow, with interest. Your future is now tied to your past decisions.
That's why debt creates pressure. It tells you that you don't fully own your time, you don't fully control your choices and you don't have margin.
Now bring that into your inner world. Most men aren't just making payments financially. They're making payments emotionally.
We feel like we owe approval, validation, success, control, reputation and comfort. So we live paying debts God never asked us to carry.
When you believe you owe the world something, you will live enslaved to its expectations.
Financial debt isn't dangerous just because you owe. It's dangerous because of interest. The longer you carry it, the more it grows.
Same thing spiritually. You start with "I just want to be respected." Then it grows into "I can't fail," "I have to keep this image," "I need to stay in control."
Now you're not just living. You're servicing a life. Every decision gets filtered through "What will they think?" and "What if I lose this?"
That's not freedom. That's interest compounding on the inside.
Romans 12 says to offer your body. That's a full transfer. Not a lease. Not partial ownership. Not shared control.
But most men live like this: "God has my Sunday, but I still manage the rest."
So now you're caught in a split system, a Kingdom identity with worldly obligations. That tension feels like constant pressure, because it is.
You don't feel exhausted because life is hard. You feel exhausted because you're paying for a version of life God never financed.
Romans 13:8 doesn't just remove debt. It redefines it. Owe nothing except love.
You are no longer driven by obligation, but by overflow. Not "I have to prove something," but "I get to live from something."

Jesus isn't inviting you into better money management. He's inviting you into ownership clarity. When your life is surrendered, you stop borrowing identity from the world, stop financing your worth through performance and stop living on approval credit.
And for the first time, you're actually free.

items: Where am I making "payments" to maintain something God never asked me to carry?
Whose approval am I still paying interest on?
What part of my life have I kept "leased" instead of fully surrendered?
show me where I've been living on borrowed identity,
trying to pay back expectations, pressure and approval.
Break the agreements I've made with false obligations.
Teach me what it means to live fully surrendered,
not managing my life, but trusting You with it.
I release every debt You didn't give me,
and I receive the freedom You already paid for.
